name: Erlang
summary: Dynamically typed functional language from Ericsson built around lightweight isolated processes, asynchronous message passing, links/monitors and supervision ('let it crash'), with hot code loading and transparent distribution. It runs on the BEAM virtual machine and ships with the OTP libraries and design principles.

level_notes.0: Erlang/OTP (erlang/otp) is the reference implementation: the compiler is written in Erlang (lib/compiler, with the scanner/parser/linter in lib/stdlib), the BEAM emulator, JIT (BeamAsm) and runtime in C/C++ under erts/. AtomVM and Firefly are independent BEAM-compatible implementations; HiPE (native compiler) was removed in OTP 24.
level_notes.1: No formal standard. The 'Erlang Reference Manual' in the OTP documentation is the normative description of the current language; changes go through Erlang Enhancement Proposals (EEPs). The 1999 'Erlang 4.7.3 Reference Manual' draft (Barklund & Virding) is the only attempt at a full specification and is long outdated; Core Erlang has its own specification.
level_notes.2: Official user's guides (Getting Started, Programming Examples, Efficiency Guide, OTP Design Principles, Interoperability Tutorial) and the ERTS/compiler internal documentation are listed at level 2.
